paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: Illustrating the empirical generalization errors and sharpness measures with respect to QLoRA weights. (<ref>) Smaller adapters with a rank of 16 achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima. (<ref>) An ensemble of k adapters leads to lower generalization errors and Hessian traces. Here, we fix the sum of the dimensions of k adapters to be equal to 256. (<ref>) QLoRA, which is trained on a quantized base model, yields lower generalization errors and Hessian trace values compared to LoRA.

model_annotations.English: This bar chart illustrates generalization errors for two methods, LoRA and QLoRA, across different rank values. The horizontal axis represents the “Rank” with categories labeled 4, 16, 64, and 256, displayed in ascending order, while the vertical axis represents the error value, labeled as a linear scale ranging from 0.3 to 0.9 with tick marks at 0.3 increments. For each rank, there are two bars: a blue bar representing “LoRA” and a green bar representing “QLoRA”. At Rank 4, the LoRA bar reaches approximately 0.55, while the QLoRA bar reaches approximately 0.50. For Rank 16, LoRA is approximately 0.61 and QLoRA is approximately 0.45. At Rank 64, LoRA is approximately 0.67 and QLoRA is approximately 0.55. Lastly, for Rank 256, LoRA is approximately 0.73 and QLoRA is around 0.65. Additionally, each bar is accompanied by a black error bar indicating variability, with the error bars being relatively consistent in length across the different ranks. No bars are visually emphasized with annotation, shading, or bolding.
model_annotations.German: This bar chart illustrates generalization error for two methods, LoRA and QLoRA, across different rank values. The horizontal axis represents “Rank” with categories 4, 16, 64, and 256, displayed in ascending order; the axis is labeled “Rank” and has a linear scale. The vertical axis represents the generalization error, labeled as a numeric scale ranging from 0.3 to 0.9 with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. For each rank value, there are two bars representing LoRA (blue) and QLoRA (green). Each bar also includes an error bar extending vertically above its upper edge. The LoRA bars at ranks 4, 16, 64, and 256 are approximately 0.56, 0.63, 0.65 and 0.66 in height, respectively. The QLoRA bars at ranks 4, 16, 64, and 256 are approximately 0.53, 0.51, 0.55, and 0.61 in height, respectively. The bars are grouped by rank, with LoRA appearing to the left and QLoRA to the right for each rank category. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotation.
